national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today distributed more than 51,000 appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various Government Organisations at the 20th Rozgar Mela this afternoon through video conferencing. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Modi emphasized the pivotal role of youth in building a developed and self-reliant India. He said that in recent years, the Central government has consistently focused on equipping the youth with the skills and opportunities needed to prepare for the future. Prime Minister Modi said the government is also working to rapidly expand employment opportunities in the private sector. He said, with this objective, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana has been launched with an outlay of around one lakh crore. The scheme is expected to enable nearly two crore young people to enter the workforce for the first time. Prime Minister Modi said that India has signed Free Trade Agreements with nearly 40 countries in the past few years, which is opening new doors of opportunity for the country’s youth. He said, such trade agreements pave the way for new partnerships and markets for country’s entrepreneurs, and create new career possibilities for the youth. Prime Minister Modi said that India is today the world’s third largest startup ecosystem. In Kolkata, Union Minister of State Education and DoNER Dr Sukanta Majumder today distributed appointment letters to newly recruited candidates during the Rozgar Mela held at National Library. The candidates were given appointment to various departments and ministries including Railway, India Posts, Health and Family Welfare. Rozgar Mela has also been organised in Howrah district where appointment letters were delivered to candidates by Union Minister of State for Ports Shipping and Waterways Shantanu Thakur. In Mumbai, Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse distributed appointment letters to newly recruited candidates at the Birla Matushri Sabhagar. Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Mumbai, Alok Kumar, and Central Board of Direct Taxes member Pankaj Kumar Mishra were also present. Addressing the newly appointed candidates, Minister Khadse urged them to continuously upgrade their skills and adapt to technological changes. She emphasised the importance of learning throughout their careers and encouraged the recruits to understand their responsibilities and keep developing themselves while serving in government departments. In another programme in Mumbai, the Principal Chief Commissioner of Customs, Mumbai Customs Zone-I, distributed appointment letters to 214 new recruits at SNDT Women’s University, Churchgate Campus. The programme highlighted the role of government service in national development and the contribution expected from the newly appointed youth towards strengthening the Indian economy. The newly appointed candidates will join various ministries and departments of the Government of India, including Revenue, Railways, Home Affairs, Health and Family Welfare, Financial Services and Defence. In Thane, Union Minister of State, Prataprao Jadhav distributed appointment letters to the newly recruited candidates. The programme was attended by Chief Income Tax Commissioner Dr. Sarita Mishra Kolhe, IIT Bombay Registrar Ganesh Bhorkade and representatives of the Survey of India. In Pune, Rozgar Mela was organised by the Customs Department. Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Murlidhar Mohol and Chief Commissioner of CGST and Customs Neeraj Kandal were present. Appointment letters were handed over to 217 candidates appointed in departments including DRDO, Customs, Airports Authority of India, the Postal Department, GAIL, Railways and CBIC. Mr. Mohol said that joining Central Government service would provide the young recruits with an opportunity to serve citizens, improve public services and contribute to innovation and research in the country. In Nagpur, Rozgar Mela event was organised at the National Fire Service College in Rajnagar. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari distributed appointment letters to 25 newly recruited candidates in a representative ceremony. A total of 337 candidates from Nagpur received appointment letters for departments including Income Tax, Railways, the Postal Department, Airports Authority of India, AIIMS and Bank of Baroda. Addressing the newly appointed candidates, Mr. Gadkari urged them to develop their professional skills and work with sensitivity towards the public while serving in the administration. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today distributed more than 51,000 appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various Government Organisations at the 20th Rozgar Mela via video conferencing.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 94 Nepalese Finance Minister Wagle Calls for Renewed India-Nepal Partnership
national_raw_news.content: Nepalese Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle has stated that India and Nepal have an opportunity to renew their partnership by building on the strong ties that already exist. Addressing an International Seminar on ‘Reimagining India-Nepal Relations in an Emerging Global Order’ organized by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS) in New Delhi today, Dr Wagle emphasised the importance of strengthening connectivity and economic cooperation and realising the considerable potential that the two countries can achieve together. Speaking exclusively to Akashvani News, the Nepalese Finance Minister also stressed upon urgent pre-disaster investments, including early warning systems and resilient infrastructure, to mitigate climate risks. On energy cooperation and cross-border electricity trade, Dr Wagle highlighted ongoing joint projects supported by Indian investments. Dr Wagle also commended India’s prompt relief and rescue assistance following recent flash floods in Nepal. He further informed that Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah is expected to visit India by the end of this year. Additional Secretary (North) at the Ministry of External Affairs, Munu Mahawar, also highlighted the need for greater ambition in taking forward the India-Nepal partnership. He noted that the two countries have made significant progress in areas such as connectivity and power, while emphasising the opportunity to advance more ambitious projects and initiatives that have remained unrealised for decades. He underlined that the potential of the relationship is much larger and therefore calls for greater ambition in goal-setting. In his welcome address, Director General of RIS, Professor Sachin Kumar Sharma highlighted the strong complementarities that exist between India and Nepal across trade, energy, education, health and development cooperation. He emphasised the need to deepen engagement so that the relationship can move from proximity to prosperity and ultimately towards shared prosperity.

national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | Sports 99 20th Asian Games Officially Opened at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan
national_raw_news.content: The 20th Asian Games officially got underway today at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan, with Emperor Naruhito declaring the Games open. The two-hour ceremony was attended by Japan’s royal family, Games officials, and Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani. India’s 501-member contingent was led by double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat during the athletes’ parade. Sehrawat replaced shot putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor as flag-bearer after the latter did not receive his ceremonial kit on time. Some events have already begun, including women’s cricket, where India have already advanced to the semifinals after an eight-wicket win over Japan yesterday. India will face Bangladesh in the second semifinal in Nisshin, Japan, tomorrow. In Teqball, which is making its Asian Games debut, India’s Quimcy D’Souza suffered a 1-2 defeat to Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in the women’s singles semifinal and will play Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto for bronze medal tomorrow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended his best wishes to the Indian contingent as the Asian Games commenced today in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. In his message, Mr Modi said each athlete has worked incredibly hard and shown remarkable dedication and determination and India is proud of them. He hoped that the athletes play well and shine at the Games.

national_raw_news.title: Union Minister L Murugan Distributes Appointment Letters to 285 newly recruited candidates in Chennai 1 hour ago 7
national_raw_news.content: In Chennai, Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting, Dr L Murugan today distributed appointment letters to 285 newly recruited candidates selected for various Central Government Ministries, Departments, and organisations. Speaking during the event, the Minister said that the newly recruited youth entering Government service would play an important role in achieving the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He urged the recruits to view their responsibilities not merely as securing employment, but as an opportunity to serve the nation and contribute to its holistic development. Mr Murugan emphasised that honesty, accountability, empathy, and a humane approach towards the public should remain integral to public service. Dr Murugan noted that the unemployment rate has declined from 6 per cent to 3.2 percent as a result of various initiatives undertaken by the Government. He also pointed out that the number of startups in the country has risen from 400 in 2014 to more than 2.5 lakh, noting that a significant number of startup founders are youth below the age of 30. The Minister added that more than 12.75 lakh appointment letters have been distributed through Rozgar Melas so far, reflecting the Government’s dedicated emphasis on creating employment opportunities for the youth.
